transcript:
[Doctor]: Hi, it's good to see you today. How have you been feeling recently?

[Patient]: Well, not so great, to be honest. My blood sugar has been out of control for the past three months, and it's gotten worse over the last two weeks.

[Doctor]: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me a bit more about your symptoms?

[Patient]: Sure. I've been experiencing some numbness in my feet, and I've gained weight unintentionally. Also, I've been getting up more frequently at night to use the bathroom.

[Doctor]: Hmm, I see. How often are these symptoms bothering you?

[Patient]: Every day, pretty much. It's really making it hard for me to walk and do anything that requires standing for a long time.

[Doctor]: I understand. Have you noticed any changes in your mood or how you're feeling emotionally?

[Patient]: No, I haven't noticed any changes in my mood or affect.

[Doctor]: Alright, thank you for sharing that. Let me take a look at your vital signs. Your blood pressure today is 135 over 85 millimeters of mercury. Your weight is 160 pounds, and your height is 5 feet 3 inches, which gives you a BMI of 28.3.

[Patient]: Okay.

[Doctor]: Now, let's do a quick examination. I'll start with your feet. Can you feel this? (Doctor performs foot exam.)

[Patient]: Not really, it feels a bit numb.

[Doctor]: It looks like you have diminished sensation and signs of early neuropathy, but no ulcers, which is good. Let's also take a look at your eyes. (Doctor performs eye exam.)

[Patient]: Alright.

[Doctor]: Your eye exam looks normal, and there are no signs of diabetic retinopathy, which is positive news.

[Patient]: That's a relief.

[Doctor]: I see from your records that your last Hemoglobin A1c was 9.2% three months ago. We need to reassess it today along with some other tests like a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests, and a Doppler Ultrasound of your lower extremities.

[Patient]: Got it.

[Doctor]: Based on what you've told me and the exam results, I can confirm that your Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus is not well controlled. Your symptoms suggest hyperglycemia, and the numbness in your feet indicates early signs of peripheral neuropathy. We need to take action to manage this better and prevent further complications.

[Patient]: What do we need to do?

[Doctor]: We're going to update your medication regimen. You'll continue to take Metformin, 1000 milligrams twice a day. I'll also add Canagliflozin, 100 milligrams once a day. Lastly, you'll start Insulin Lispro, 10 units before each meal.

[Patient]: That sounds like a lot. Will it help?

[Doctor]: Yes, these medications should help bring your blood sugar levels under control. We’ll monitor your progress closely. In addition to the medications, I recommend making some lifestyle changes.

[Patient]: What kind of changes?

[Doctor]: For diet, you should follow a structured low-sugar, high-fiber meal plan. I'll provide you with detailed dietary guidelines. For exercise, aim to cycle for 30 minutes a day, five days a week.

[Patient]: Okay, I can try that.

[Doctor]: Also, though you mentioned you don’t smoke, I recommend a referral to a smoking cessation program with Nurse Practitioner Lisa Green, just in case you need support in the future. Limit your alcohol intake to one drink per week.

[Patient]: I don't smoke, but the alcohol recommendation makes sense.

[Doctor]: Great. We’ll also refer you to a podiatrist, Dr. Anna Thompson, for diabetic foot care. We need to keep a close watch on your feet given the early neuropathy.

[Patient]: Alright, I understand.

[Doctor]: I’ll schedule a follow-up visit in two weeks to monitor your blood glucose levels and assess how the insulin is working.

[Patient]: Two weeks sounds good.

[Doctor]: I’ll also order a new Hemoglobin A1c test, a Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests, and a Doppler Ultrasound of your lower extremities to check blood flow.

[Patient]: Okay, I’ll get those done.

[Doctor]: It's crucial to maintain glycemic control to prevent complications. These tests will help us evaluate your overall health and how well the treatment is working.

[Patient]: I want to make sure I'm doing everything I can.

[Doctor]: That’s the right attitude. Here are some educational materials on diet and exercise to help you get started. Do you have any questions about the treatment plan?

[Patient]: No, I think you covered everything. Thank you for explaining it all.

[Doctor]: You're welcome. If you have any questions or concerns before the follow-up visit, don’t hesitate to call. Let's work together to get your diabetes under control.

[Patient]: Thank you, Doctor. I appreciate your help.

[Doctor]: My pleasure. Take care, and I'll see you in two weeks.

[Patient]: See you then.

[Doctor]: Goodbye.

[Patient]: Goodbye.
